get.summary: Readiness probe: 200 when the server can serve requests, 503 otherwise.
Accounts (at most 200).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a name or email.

delete.summary:
Delete an account (GDPR erasure). Refused while it owns a company
organization (transfer it with the owner's API, or delete it first).

patch.summary:
Make or unmake an instance admin, suspend or lift (never leaving the
instance without an active admin).

get.summary: The instance-wide identity providers.

post.summary: Add an instance-wide identity provider (full sessions for its logins).

delete.summary: Delete an instance-wide identity provider, and the identities linked through it.

get.summary: Every background job with its last 10 runs.

post.summary: Run a job now, in the background. Returns its run (`running`).

get.summary: Organizations (at most 200), with their owner, members, quota, usage.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a name or email.

post.summary: Create an organization owned by an existing account.

delete.summary:
Delete an organization (personal ones included): its data at once, its
stored chunks with the garbage collection, started now.

patch.summary: Rename, set the quota, suspend or lift, set the default storage.

get.summary: Every setting: its stored value (or none: the default), default, description.

patch.summary:
Change settings (`null`: back to the default), all or none: the result is
validated as a whole, then applied at once (no restart).

get.summary: The shared storages, with their usage.

post.summary: Add a shared storage, tested first (write, read back, delete).
Make a shared storage the instance default (new libraries go there).

get.summary: The account's app passwords.

post.summary:
Create an app password, within what this session reaches (a restricted
session: inside its organization). The password is shown only once.

delete.summary: Revoke an app password: refused at once.

get.summary: The account's ways to log in.

delete.summary: Remove one of the account's ways to log in (never the last one).

post.summary:
Log in with email and password. Sets the session cookie. Unknown email and
wrong password give the same error, in the same time.

Log out: revokes this session at once if it's still valid, and clears the
cookie in any case. No session needed: an expired or revoked session's
cookie would otherwise stay, as only the server clears an `httpOnly`
cookie. A valid session stays protected by the CSRF rule (a `POST`, never
a `GET` another site could trigger). App passwords can't log out.

get.summary:
The instance-wide providers, for the login page. An organization's
provider isn't listed: the organization shares its start link.

The provider sends the user back here: opens a session (or links the
identity), then redirects to the web app.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Set by the provider when the user refused, or on errors.

post.summary:
Start linking a provider's identity to this account: returns the URL to
send the browser to. A POST (CSRF-protected), not a link: another site must
not be able to start a linking flow in the user's browser.

get.summary: Start logging in with a provider: redirects to it.

post.summary:
Change the password (a full session, the current one asked): every other
session is logged out, this one kept. Failed attempts count as failed
logins. Without a password (OIDC only), the reset email sets one.

404.description: `no_password`: set one through the reset email

post.summary: Email a link to choose a new password. Always `202`.

Choose a new password (the link's token). Also confirms the address, and
logs out every session. TOTP, if on, stays required.

Create an account (when registration is open): it gets a personal
organization, and logs in once its address is confirmed by email. Always
`202`: a taken address gets an email saying so instead.

get.summary: The account's live sessions.

delete.summary: Revoke one of the account's sessions (e.g. a lost device).

post.summary:
The email a reset or invitation link is for, without using it: the page
choosing a password scores it against the email. Holding the token proves
the inbox, so the address tells nothing new.

Start setting up TOTP: a new secret, not required at login until
confirmed. Starting again replaces an unconfirmed secret.

Confirm TOTP with a first code: from now on, password logins ask for a
code. Returns the recovery codes (shown only now).
Turn TOTP off, with a current code (or a recovery code).

New recovery codes, with a current code (or a recovery code): the
previous ones stop working.
Confirm an email address (the link's token): the account can log in, and is.
Send the confirmation email again (unverified accounts). Always `202`.

Mark uploaded chunks as ready, after checking each object exists with the
declared size. Returns the chunks still to upload (object missing): request
new URLs for them (same declaration).

Cancel an upload: tombstones the given chunks that no version references.
Their objects are deleted later, once their upload URLs have expired.

Which chunks to upload. Misses become pending chunks; every chunk returned is
touched (repeat the lookup as a keepalive during long uploads).

Declare what will be uploaded and get presigned upload URLs (in batches).
The declaration is fixed at the first request; the URL only accepts exactly
the declared bytes (their SHA-256 is signed). Checks the organization's quota.

Commit versions: each a new file (`parent` + `name`) or a new version
(`file`), in its own transaction, so one failing never undoes the others.
The outcomes come in the request's order; one commit is a batch of one.
An outcome's error: `name_taken`, `chunk_missing` (with the chunks to
upload again), `chunk_not_allowed`, `not_found` (file, folder, base
version), `invalid_target`.

Files' chunks, in order, with presigned download URLs: each file's current
version, or the one asked. The outcomes come in the request's order.

get.summary: A file's content, streamed (previews and downloads in the browser).

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: A version of the file (default: the current one).

get.summary: A file's versions: a tree (branches after conflicts and restores).

post.summary: Make an old version current. The next commit based on it branches the tree.

get.summary:
What a login page shows before anyone logs in: the instance's name, and
whether accounts can be created (registration open, and emails sendable).

post.summary:
Accept an invitation (the link's token): joins the organization. A new
account chooses its password here, and is logged in; an account that can
already log in just joins (no login: its own password and TOTP apply).

get.summary: The libraries the user is a member of.

post.summary:
Create a library: its root folder, the creator as `write` member, in the given
namespaces. Storage: the organization's default, else the instance default.

409.description: Name taken, or no storage configured

delete.summary:
Put a library, with everything in it, in its organization's trash (a
`write` member); or (`permanent`, from the trash) delete it for good.

parameters.name: permanent
parameters.description: Delete for good (a library already in the trash only).

get.summary: A library's members (its members, and the organization's owner).

put.summary:
Give a member of the organization access to the library, or change its
role (the owner). Invited members not joined yet can be added: their
access is ready when they accept.

404.description: No such library, or no such member of its organization

delete.summary:
Take a member's access to the library away (the owner). A library may be
left without members: nobody reaches it until it's given some.

post.summary:
Take a library out of the trash (renamed ` (restored)` if its name was
taken since).

get.summary: A library's trash.

The instance's limits, as they stand (they change live): clients size their
work by them, e.g. an upload engine's window.
The logged-in account and its organizations.

delete.summary:
Delete this account (a full session, confirmed with its password if it has
one and its TOTP code if on): its personal organization, memberships,
identities, tokens and emails, at once. Refused while it owns a company
organization (transfer or delete it first).

get.summary:
Everything the server holds about this account, never secrets (a full
session). Files come through the usual paths (CLI, WebDAV).

delete.summary:
Delete a namespace (the owner): its libraries stop deduplicating with each
other at once, and keep every chunk they already share.

put.summary:
Put one of the organization's libraries in the namespace (the owner):
from now on, it dedups with the namespace's other libraries, both ways.
Every member of each can then probe the others' content: a security
decision (decisions.md, Trust boundary).

delete.summary:
Take a library out of the namespace (the owner): the trust is revoked at
once; the library keeps the chunks it already shares.

patch.summary:
Rename and/or move files and folders, each in its own transaction, each
its own outcome. Within a library a move is one row; to another library of
the same organization, the subtree (and its history) follows.

200.description: Each node's outcome, in order: errors `root`, `not_found`, `name_taken`, `move_into_itself`, `other_organization`

post.summary:
Copy files and folders into folders of any library of the same
organization, each in its own transaction, each its own outcome. Files
keep their current version only, sharing its chunks.

200.description: Each copy's outcome, in order (`node`: the copy): errors `not_found`, `name_taken`, `other_organization`

post.summary:
Take files and folders out of the trash, each in its own transaction,
each its own outcome: back in their folder, or into the library's root if
that one is trashed too; renamed if their name is taken.

200.description: Each node's outcome, in order: errors `not_found`

post.summary:
Put files and folders in the trash, or (`permanent`, from the trash)
delete them for good with their subtrees and histories; each in its own
transaction, each its own outcome.

200.description: Each node's outcome, in order (no `node`): errors `root`, `not_found`

get.summary: A file or folder, with its library and path.
A folder's children.

post.summary:
Create folders below a folder, like `mkdir -p`: each path's missing
folders created, existing ones kept, all in one transaction. Each path's
folder, in order.

get.summary:
A folder's whole subtree (outside the trash) in one streamed answer: NDJSON,
one `{"node": ...}` line per node, parents before their children, then
`{"end": {"count": n}}`, or `{"error": ...}` if it fails midway. A stream
without its end line was cut.

post.summary:
Create a company organization, owned by the account (from a full session;
instance admins only when `organization_creation` is `admins`).

get.summary: An organization, with its quota and usage (any member).

delete.summary:
Delete the organization (the owner): every library, file and version at
once; the stored data follows with the garbage collection, started now.

get.summary: The organization's identity providers (the owner).

post.summary:
Add an identity provider for the organization (the owner): its logins open
sessions restricted to the organization. `https` issuers on public
addresses only; the secret as a value (stored encrypted).

delete.summary:
Delete one of the organization's identity providers, and the identities
linked through it (the owner).

patch.summary: Change one of the organization's identity providers (the owner).

get.summary:
Every library of the organization, whether the owner is a member or not
(the owner).
The organization's members and pending invitations (any member).

post.summary:
Add a member by email (the owner): an existing account joins at once (and
is told by email); another address gets an invitation.

delete.summary: Remove a member, or cancel an invitation (the owner; never the owner).

get.summary: The organization's dedup namespaces and their libraries (the owner).

post.summary: Create a dedup namespace, empty (the owner).
Give the organization to another joined member (the owner).

404.description: Not the owner, or not a joined member

get.summary: An organization's trashed libraries (those the account is a member of).

Files and folders by name (case-insensitive), in the libraries the user
reaches, outside the trash. At most 50.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a name (at least 3 characters).

get.summary: Whether the instance still has to be set up.

post.summary:
Set up a fresh instance, once: the admin (logged in by the answer), the
first organization, and the storages, each tested first (write, read back,
delete). The token goes in `X-Theca-Setup-Token`.

get.summary: Server version and supported API majors.

email.description: An existing account joins at once; another address gets an invitation.

AdminAccount.description: An account, for the instance admin.

suspended.description: Suspended: it can't log in, its tokens are refused.

AdminOrganization.description: An organization, for the instance admin.

suspended.description: Suspended: nothing in it is reachable.

name.description: Its name (empty for the library's root).

ApiError.description: An API error: a stable machine-readable `code` and a human message.

AppPassword.description: An app password (never the secret itself, except once at creation).

last_seen.description: Last used (precise to a few minutes), if ever.

library.description: The library it's limited to, if any.

organization.description: The organization it's limited to, if any.

ChangePassword.description: A password change: the current one, and the new one.

new.description: The new password (at least 8 characters, and strong enough).

ChunkState.description: Whether a chunk must be uploaded.

ChunkUrl.description: A presigned URL for one chunk.

headers.description: Headers to send with the request, exactly (they are signed).

url.description: Where to `PUT` (upload) or `GET` (download) it, without authentication.

Commit.description:
One commit of `POST /files/commit`: either `file` (a new version of an existing file) or
`parent` + `name` (a new file).

base_version.description: The version the client started from (none for a new file).

name.description: The name of a new file.

parent.description: The folder of a new file.

CommitOutcome.description: One commit's outcome in a batch: committed, or why not.

status.description: With `error`: its HTTP status, as a call of its own would have answered.

Commits.description:
`POST /files/commit`: commits, each in its own transaction (one
commit is a batch of one).

conflict.description: The base wasn't the current version: another branch exists.

unchanged.description:
The same content as the base, still current: no version was created,
`version` is the current one.

id.description: The file or folder to copy.

parent.description: The folder to copy into (in any library of the same organization).

replace.description:
A file of that name exists there: the copy is a new version of it
(based on its current one). Otherwise `name_taken`. Folders are never
replaced.

CopyNodes.description: `POST /nodes/copy`: copies, each in its own transaction (at most 1000).

nodes.description: The copies, each its own outcome.

CreateAppPassword.description: Create an app password (CLI, API clients, WebDAV): data access only.

library.description: Limit it to one library (its organization implied).

name.description: Shown in lists, e.g. "laptop CLI" (1 to 200 characters).

organization.description:
Limit it to one organization (none: the whole account; a restricted
session: always its own organization).

read_only.description: Read only, whatever the account's role in the libraries.

CreateFolders.description:
`POST /nodes/{parent}/folders`: folders to create in a folder, like
`mkdir -p` (missing ones created, existing ones kept).

paths.description: Paths relative to the folder, `/`-separated (`a`, `a/b`); at most 1000.

name.description: The library name (same rules as file names).

namespaces.description:
Existing namespaces of the organization to put the library in. Empty:
the library only dedups with itself.

organization.description: The organization that will own it (the account must be a member).

owner.description: The email of an existing account, its owner.

Declare.description:
One chunk of `POST /chunks/upload-urls`: what the client will upload. Fixed
at the first request; a later request (expired URL) must repeat it exactly.

chunk.description: A pending chunk from the lookup.

stored_sha256.description: SHA-256 of those bytes: the upload URL only accepts exactly them.

stored_size.description: Size of the bytes to upload (after compression), at most `plain_size`.

DeleteAccount.description:
`DELETE /me`: the account confirms (its password if it has one, its TOTP
code if on).

Download.description: A file's version to download (an outcome of `POST /files/download`).

DownloadChunk.description: One chunk of a download, in order.

hash.description: Its hash, to verify the downloaded plaintext.

DownloadFile.description: A file to download: its current version, or another one.

version.description: One of its versions (default: the current one).

DownloadOutcome.description: One file's outcome in `POST /files/download`: its chunks, or why not.

oneOf.description: Refused, and why (`not_found`: the file or the version).

Downloads.description: `POST /files/download`: files whose chunks to download (at most 100).

Export.description:
Everything the server holds about an account (`GET /me/export`), never
secrets. Files come through the usual paths (CLI, WebDAV).

files.description: The files of its personal organization.

ExportedAccount.description: The account part of an export.

FolderPath.description: A folder of `POST /nodes/{parent}/folders`, in the request's order.

created.description: Created by this request (false: it existed).

Health.description: Health report. The contract is the HTTP status (200 / 503); the body is informational.

checks.description: Each check: `ok` or `failing`. Details go to the logs, never here.

failing_jobs.description:
Background jobs whose last 3 runs failed (reported, not a failed probe:
restarting the server wouldn't fix them).

Identity.description: One of the account's ways to log in.

IdentityProvider.description: An OIDC provider users can log in with.

password_strength.description:
The zxcvbn score a new password needs, 0 (none: 8 characters only) to 4
(the setting `password_strength`).

registration.description: Accounts can be created (`registration = open`, and SMTP configured).

JobRun.description: One run of a background job.

JobStatus.description: A background job and its last runs (admin).

interval_secs.description: How often it runs, in seconds.

writable.description:
Whether the account may write in it: its role, within its credential's
scope and read-only cap.

joined.description: False while it's an invitation not accepted yet.

Limits.description: `GET /limits`: the instance's limits clients size their work by.

max_pending_uploads.description:
Chunks an account may have declared and not yet announced
(`max_pending_uploads`): an upload engine's window.

LinkToken.description: A token from an email's link.

totp.description:
The current TOTP code (or a recovery code), if TOTP is on. Without it,
a right password gets `totp_required`: ask for the code, send again.

plain_size.description: Size of the plaintext (at most 8 MiB).

chunk.description: The chunk to reference in the commit.

Me.description: The logged-in account and its organizations.

can_create_organizations.description:
It may create company organizations (the setting
`organization_creation`, or an instance admin; a full session).

totp.description: Whether logging in with the password also asks for a TOTP code.

Member.description: A member of an organization (or a pending invitation).

id.description: The member (their user in this organization).

Membership.description: An account's membership in an organization.

joined.description: False while it's an invitation not accepted yet.

owner.description: The account owns it (its administrator: members, settings).

personal.description: The account's personal organization (shown as "My files").

suspended.description: Suspended by the instance admin: nothing in it is reachable.

Namespace.description: A dedup namespace: its libraries' members trust each other.

NewAppPassword.description: A new app password: the secret is shown only this once.

password.description: Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <password>` (or WebDAV Basic auth).

NewStorage.description: A storage backend. Credentials are paths to files on the server, never values.

current_version.description: A file's current version (the base of a new one).

size.description:
A file's size in bytes (its current version's); none for a folder or a
file without a version yet.

NodeInfo.description: A file or folder, with where it is.

ancestors.description:
The folders above it, from the library's root (named `""`) to its
folder; none for the root.

path.description: Its path in the library, e.g. `/a/b.txt` (`/` for the root).

size.description:
A file's size in bytes (its current version's); none for a folder or a
file without a version yet.

NodeOutcome.description:
One node's outcome in a batch: the node as it is now (none after a trash),
or why not.

oneOf.description: Done: the node now (renamed, moved, the copy); none for a trash.

status.description: With `error`: its HTTP status, as a call of its own would have answered.

OidcRedirect.description: Where to send the browser to continue with an OIDC provider.

Organization.description: An organization, to one of its members.

personal.description: The account's personal organization (shown as "My files").

quota.description: Its quota in bytes; none: unlimited.

used.description: What it stores, in bytes (counted against the quota).

OrganizationLibrary.description: One of an organization's libraries, to its owner.

members.description: How many members it has (none: nobody reaches it until given some).

ProviderInfo.description: An OIDC identity provider (never its secret).

client_secret_file.description: The client secret's file (instance-wide providers using one).

id.description: The provider: its login starts at `/api/v1/auth/oidc/{id}/start`.

issuer.description: The issuer (its discovery document is under it).

ProviderRequest.description: Creates or changes an OIDC identity provider (changes: only the fields given).

client_secret.description:
The client secret's value (stored encrypted). An organization's
provider takes only this.

client_secret_file.description: A path to a file holding the client secret (instance-wide only).

issuer.description: The issuer URL (an organization's: `https`, public addresses only).

RecoveryCodes.description:
One-time recovery codes, each usable once instead of a TOTP code. Shown
only now: the server only keeps their hashes.

email.description: The email (verified before the account can log in).

RestoreNodes.description:
`POST /nodes/restore`: files and folders out of the trash, each in its own
transaction (at most 1000).

nodes.description: The trashed files and folders, each its own outcome.

RestoreOutcome.description: One restore's outcome in a batch.

status.description: With `error`: its HTTP status, as a call of its own would have answered.

name.description: Its name (` (restored)` added if the old one was taken).

parent.description: Its folder: its old one, or the library's root if that one is in the trash.

Role.description: A member's role in a library.

size.description:
A file's size in bytes (its current version's); none for a folder or a
file without a version yet.

Session.description: A live session of the account.

ip.description: The address it was opened from.

restricted_to.description: The organization it is restricted to, if opened through an organization's identity provider.

user_agent.description: The browser or client that opened it.

SetPassword.description: A token from an email's link, and a password to set.

password.description:
The new password (at least 8 characters, and strong enough: the
instance's `password_strength`). Optional to accept an
invitation for an account that can already log in.

SetRole.description: `PUT /libraries/{id}/members/{user}`: adds the member, or changes its role.

value.description: Its stored value (none: the default applies).

Setup.description: Sets up a fresh instance: its admin, first organization and storages.

admin_password.description: The instance admin's password (at least 8 characters).

organization.description: The first organization, owned by the admin.

storages.description:
One or more storages, shared by the instance. The first one is the
default (new libraries go there).

SetupStatus.description: Whether the instance still has to be set up.

required.description: Not set up yet: the server only serves the setup.

token_required.description: The setup needs the token printed in the server's logs.

access_key_file.description: Path to a file holding the access key.

path_style.description: Path-style URLs (`host/bucket/key`), what self-hosted servers usually need.

secret_key_file.description: Path to a file holding the secret key.

StorageBackend.description: A storage implementation and its settings.

StorageInfo.description: A storage backend, for the instance admin.

default.description: The instance default (new libraries go there).

TokenEmail.description: The account an email's link is for.

TotpCode.description: A TOTP code (6 digits), or a recovery code where accepted.

TotpSetup.description: A TOTP secret being set up (not required at login until confirmed).

secret.description: The secret in base32, to type into an authenticator app.

uri.description: The `otpauth://` URI, to show as a QR code.

member.description: The joined member becoming the owner.

size.description:
A file's size in bytes (its current version's); none for a folder or a
file without a version yet.

TrashNodes.description:
`POST /nodes/trash`: files and folders to the trash, or (`permanent`,
already in the trash) deleted for good; each in its own transaction (at
most 1000).

nodes.description: The files and folders, each its own outcome.

permanent.description: Delete for good (nodes already in the trash only).

TrashedLibrary.description: A library in its organization's trash.

oneOf.description: A node, parents before their children.

node.description: A node, parents before their children.

TreeLine.description:
One line of `GET /nodes/{id}/tree` (NDJSON): a node, then the end (with
how many nodes came) or an error. A stream without its end line is cut.

path.description: Its path below the listed folder (`a`, `a/b.txt`).

size.description:
A file's size in bytes (its current version's); none for a folder or a
file without a version yet.

instance_admin.description: Make or unmake an instance admin (never the last one).

name.description: The new name (same rules as file names).

parent.description: The new folder (in any library of the same organization).

replace.description:
A file of that name exists there: merge into it (its history gains
this file's versions after its current one, this file's current version
